title: Finite-order elements in an integral ring cannot be congruent to one at level at least three
statement: Let $R$ be a unital associative ring, not necessarily commutative, whose additive group is free of finite rank over $\mathbf Z$ (that is, it has a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]). Let $n\geq3$ and $r\geq1$ be integers and let $u,b\in R$. If $u^r=1$ and $u=1+n b$, where $n b$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $b$, then $u=1$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 14.5, printed p.63, and the eigenvalue argument of Proposition 14.4(b), printed p.62: general finite-free-ring formulation using its left regular representation; the finite-order conclusion uses characteristic-zero semisimplicity.

proof.text: Choose a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $R$ using [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For $x\in R$, let $M_x\in M_d(\mathbf Z)$ have column $j$ the coordinates of $xe_j$. Associativity and distributivity give $M_{xy}=M_xM_y$, $M_{x+y}=M_x+M_y$ and $M_1=I$. This representation is injective: $M_x=M_y$ implies $(x-y)e_j=0$ for every $j$, hence $(x-y)1=0$ by expanding $1$ in the basis, so $x=y$. If $d=0$ then $R$ is the zero ring and the conclusion holds. Otherwise put $U=M_u$, $B=M_b$; the hypotheses give $U^r=I$ and $U=I+nB$.

source.place: Proposition 14.4(b), printed p.62, integral-endomorphism argument; explicit left regular representation adaptation.

proof.text: Work on $V=\mathbf C^d$, with $U,B$ acting by the same integer matrices. The field $\mathbf C$ is algebraically closed by [lem-weil-complex-algebraically-closed]. The nonzero polynomial $p=X^r-1$ annihilates $U$ and satisfies $p\prime=rX^{r-1}$ and $p-(X/r)p\prime=-1$, since $r\ne0$ in characteristic zero. If $p=h^2k$, differentiation gives $p\prime=2hh\prime k+h^2k\prime$. Thus $h$ divides both $p$ and $p\prime$, hence divides $-1$ by the displayed identity; it cannot be nonconstant. Therefore $p$ is squarefree in the explicit sense of [lem-sfb-squarefree-annihilator-invariant-complements], which supplies invariant complements for $U$.

source.place: Proposition 14.4(b), printed p.62: characteristic-zero semisimplicity of the finite-order operator.

proof.text: For an eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $U$, choose $v\ne0$ with $Uv=\lambda v$. Induction gives $U^rv=\lambda^rv$, so $\lambda^r=1$. From $U=I+nB$ obtain $Bv=\alpha v$ for $\alpha=(\lambda-1)/n$. By [lem-weil-cayley-hamilton-free-module], $B$ on $\mathbf Z^d$ satisfies a monic $q\in\mathbf Z[X]$ of degree $d\geq1$. Applying $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf C$ to each entry preserves the finite sums and products in $q(B)=0$, so this equation also holds over $\mathbf C$. Inductively $B^iv=\alpha^iv$, whence $0=q(B)v=q(\alpha)v$. Since $v\ne0$, $q(\alpha)=0$, proving that $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer in exactly the sense of [def-weil-algebraic-integer].

source.place: Proposition 14.4(b), printed p.62: integrality of eigenvalues, made explicit by Cayley-Hamilton.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-integer-root-unity-congruence] in $K=\mathbf C$ to $\lambda=1+n\alpha$, using $n\geq3$, $r\geq1$, $\lambda^r=1$ and the integrality proved in Step 3. It gives $\lambda=1$ for every eigenvalue of $U$.

source.place: Lemma 14.5, printed p.63, applied in the eigenvalue argument of Proposition 14.4(b).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-invariant-complements-eigenspace-span], the eigenspaces of $U$ span $\mathbf C^d$, since Step 2 supplies the invariant complements. Step 4 shows that $U$ is the identity on each nonzero eigenspace, hence on their sum: $U=I$ over $\mathbf C$.

source.place: Proposition 14.4(b), printed p.62: removal of the unipotent possibility by characteristic-zero semisimplicity.

proof.text: Each entry of $U-I$ is an integer whose image in $\mathbf C$ is zero. Injectivity of $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf C$ gives $M_u=M_1$ over $\mathbf Z$. Injectivity of the explicit representation in Step 1 now gives $u=1$.

source.place: Proposition 14.4(b), printed p.62, faithfulness of the left regular representation.

proof_origin.place: Chapter I, Proposition 14.4(b), printed p.62, and Lemma 14.5, printed p.63; left regular representation and characteristic-zero semisimplicity adaptation.
